projects.title: Number Pattern Studio
projects.summary: Print number triangles and squares from a size the user types.
objectives: Use a loop inside a loop to build rows and columns
Control where print() ends a line with end=
Turn one number from input() into a whole pattern

steps.title: Read the size
steps.text: Ask for a size with input() and convert it with int().

steps.title: One loop per row
steps.text: Write a for loop over range(1, size + 1). Each pass prints one row.

steps.title: Numbers in a row
steps.text: Inside it, loop again from 1 to the row number and print each number with end=" ".

steps.title: Finish the row
steps.text: After the inner loop, call print() on its own to start the next line.

steps.title: Try other sizes
steps.text: Run it with 1, 3 and 6. A size of 1 should print a single 1.

projects.starterCode:
# Number Pattern Studio
size = int(input("Size: "))

# Print one row per number from 1 to size

projects.title: Word Statistics
projects.summary: Analyse a sentence: count its words, find the longest one and the most common one.
objectives: Split text into a list of words
Count things with a dictionary and .get()
Find a maximum while looping

steps.title: Read and split
steps.text: Read a sentence, make it lower case and split() it into words.

steps.title: Count the words
steps.text: len() of the list is the word count.

steps.title: Longest word
steps.text: Loop over the words and keep the longest seen so far (the first one wins a tie).

steps.title: Most common word
steps.text: Count every word in a dictionary with counts[w] = counts.get(w, 0) + 1, then loop to find the biggest count.

steps.title: Print a report
steps.text: Print Words, Longest and Most common, each on its own line.

projects.starterCode:
# Word Statistics
text = input("Sentence: ")
words = text.lower().split()
projects.sampleRun:
Sentence: the cat and the hat
Words: 5
Longest: the
Most common: the

projects.title: Temperature Log Analyser
projects.summary: Collect temperature readings until the user types done, skipping anything that isn't a number.
objectives: Keep reading input in a loop until a stop word
Survive bad input with try / except ValueError
Summarise a list with min(), max() and an average

steps.title: Loop until done
steps.text: Use while True and break when the user types done.

steps.title: Convert safely
steps.text: Wrap float(text) in try. In except ValueError print a short message and continue.

steps.title: Store good readings
steps.text: Append every valid number to a list.

steps.title: Handle no data
steps.text: If the list is empty at the end, print No readings and stop.

steps.title: Print the summary
steps.text: Print the count, lowest, highest and the average with :.1f.

projects.title: To-do List Saved to a File
projects.summary: Add tasks, save them to todo.txt and read them back, even when the file doesn't exist yet.
objectives: Append lines to a text file
Read a file line by line and clean each line
Handle a missing file without crashing

steps.title: Show saved tasks
steps.text: Write show_tasks(): open todo.txt in a try block and print each line with strip(). In except FileNotFoundError print No tasks yet.

steps.title: Add tasks
steps.text: Ask for tasks in a loop. Stop on an empty answer.

steps.title: Append each task
steps.text: Open todo.txt with "a" and write the task followed by \n.

steps.title: Show the list again
steps.text: Call show_tasks() once more so the new tasks appear.

steps.title: Run it twice
steps.text: Run the program again: the tasks from the first run are still in the file (in this session).

projects.title: Library System with Classes
projects.summary: Model books as objects, lend and return them, and print the library with __str__.
objectives: Design a class with attributes and methods
Keep many objects in a list and search it
Give objects a readable print form with __str__

steps.title: The Book class
steps.text: Give Book a title, an author and available = True in __init__.

steps.title: Lend and return
steps.text: lend() sets available to False and returns True, or returns False if it was already lent. give_back() sets it to True.

steps.title: Printing a book
steps.text: __str__ returns e.g. "Dune by Herbert (available)" or "(on loan)".

steps.title: The library
steps.text: Make a list of three Book objects and a find(title) function that returns the matching book or None.

steps.title: Try it
steps.text: Lend one book twice, return it, and print every book after each change.

projects.title: Calculator
projects.summary: A two-number calculator for +, -, * and / that never crashes on division by zero.
objectives: Choose an operation with if / elif
Show a friendly message instead of a ZeroDivisionError
Print results with two decimal places

steps.title: Read the numbers
steps.text: Read the first number, the operator and the second number. Convert numbers with float().

steps.title: Pick the operation
steps.text: Use if / elif for +, -, * and /.

steps.title: Protect division
steps.text: If the second number is 0 and the operator is /, print Cannot divide by zero.

steps.title: Unknown operator
steps.text: Anything else prints Unknown operator.

steps.title: Show the result
steps.text: Print Result: with :.2f, e.g. Result: 3.50.

Add up amounts per category with a dictionary
Print a tidy summary

steps.title: How many?

steps.title: Grand total

projects.title: Quiz Application
projects.summary: Ask questions stored in a list of dictionaries, accept answers in any case and show the score.
objectives: Keep quiz data separate from the quiz logic
Compare answers fairly with strip() and lower()
Report a score and a short message

steps.title: Store the questions
steps.text: Make a list of dictionaries, each with a "q" and an "a" key.

steps.title: Ask each question
steps.text: Loop over the list and ask each question with input().

steps.title: Mark the answer
steps.text: Compare answer.strip().lower() with the stored answer. Print Correct! or the right answer.

steps.title: Keep score
steps.text: Add 1 to score for every correct answer.

steps.title: Final message
steps.text: Print Score: 2/3 and Well done! when every answer was right.

projects.title: Password Generator and Checker
projects.summary: Generate random passwords with the random module, then rate how strong a password is.
objectives: Build a string one random character at a time
Check a string for digits, capitals and small letters
Turn several checks into a single rating

steps.title: Pick a character set
steps.text: Make one string with letters and digits, e.g. letters = "abc...XYZ0123456789".

steps.title: Generate
steps.text: Ask for a length and add random.choice(letters) to an empty string that many times.

steps.title: Check strength
steps.text: For the password to check, count which rules it meets: 8 or more characters, a digit, a capital, a small letter.

steps.title: Rate it
steps.text: 4 rules: Strong. 3 rules: Medium. Fewer: Weak.

steps.title: Try both
steps.text: Generate one password, then check a weak one like abc.

projects.starterCode:
# Password Generator and Checker
import random

letters = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
